events.title: Execution of Guy Fawkes
events.description: Guy Fawkes, caught guarding gunpowder beneath the House of Lords in the Gunpowder Plot of 1605, was hanged, drawn and quartered in London for his part in the conspiracy to assassinate King James I.
events.significance: The failed plot is commemorated annually in Britain as Guy Fawkes Night (Bonfire Night) on November 5 and shaped English attitudes toward Catholic dissent for generations.

events.title: U.S. Congress Passes the Thirteenth Amendment
events.description: The House of Representatives passed the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution by a vote of 119 to 56, achieving the required two-thirds majority and sending it to the states for ratification. Abolitionists and lawmakers celebrated the outcome in the chamber.
events.significance: The amendment, ratified in December 1865, abolished slavery and involuntary servitude in the United States except as punishment for a crime, marking a turning point in American history.

events.title: Birth of Franz Schubert
events.description: Austrian composer Franz Schubert was born in Vienna. He became one of the leading figures in the transition from Classical to Romantic music, composing over 600 songs (Lieder), symphonies, chamber music and piano works before dying at age 31.
events.significance: Schubert elevated the art song to new heights, and works like the Unfinished Symphony and Winterreise remain central to the classical repertoire.

events.title: Explorer 1 Launched
events.description: The United States launched Explorer 1, its first artificial satellite, from Cape Canaveral aboard a Juno I rocket. The satellite carried instruments developed by James Van Allen's team that detected radiation belts around Earth.
events.significance: Explorer 1 marked the U.S. entry into the Space Race following Sputnik and led to the discovery of the Van Allen radiation belts, a landmark finding in space science.

events.title: Nauru Gains Independence
events.description: The Pacific island of Nauru became an independent republic, ending its status as a United Nations trust territory administered by Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom.
events.significance: Nauru became the world's smallest independent republic, and its later economic story, built on phosphate mining and its subsequent decline, became a notable case study in resource dependence.
